cohorts.label: <2h refund window
cohorts.summary: Reviewers manage building power and camera feeds to survive the night.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game's mechanics require managing camera observation, audio cues, and shutting doors to defend against animatronics while carefully monitoring limited building power.

citations.review_text: This game introduces a unique system of observing the danger that lurks in the building through cameras. Then when they reach your door, you shut the door to survive. There are unique features amongst many characters like Freddy and Foxy that each require you to change your strategy entirely. This is a great start to a long lasting and impactful series. It still holds up to modern games pretty well in my opinion. Only annoying part is learning how Freddy works, as he can be extremely confusing to counter, and therefore I had browse the internet, whereas learning myself. At time you may find yourself stuck on a night and exhasuted of trying over and over again, which is can be quite frustrating, but you will eventually get past whatever night you are struggling with. Overall, this is a good game that continues to hold up to modern gaming with unique features and gameplay. Definitely a must try.

Is this a good game? Kinda. Is it a good horror experience? Absolutely. This game was an instant classic when it came out back in the day and it's not hard to figure why. It's a 1st person perspective and you are stuck in one spot in an office with two entrances on either side of you that require power to stay closed. Throughout each night you have to pay attention to the cameras, audio cues, and on occasion, you have to catch the animatronics right before they're about to strike and slam the doors shut before they can get in. However, you have to play dangerously and leave them mostly deactivated for as long as you feel you can get away with because if you use them too much, all the power in the building runs out and once any of the animatronics makes it through the door, you're murdered horribly with the most ear piercing screech ever produced audibly. It's a pretty amazing and extremely intense experience. The aggression of the animatronics goes up as the nights progress so you will start getting killed and after a while, the desperation begins to set in as you beg any god listening for the furry fatality squad to stay away for just a few seconds more. And when you make it through the night, man, there's few things more ludicrously elating than the angelic chime of the 6:00am bells. All that said, this isn't really that much of a "Game" per say. You hold still, click a few buttons, watch some cameras and wait. That's literally all that's there to do.  So I wouldn't necessarily call this one as much of a horror game so much as an interactive horror experience. Obviously it's not on the same level as like Resident Evil or Silent Hill but at the same time, it's not trying to be. FNAF is it's own thing and has been for over a decade at this point and for good reason. It's a classic and I do recommend it to any horror fans that like the intensity of a thriller.

You cant walk, check cams for foxy, do NOT run out of power, close left door for Bonnie & Foxy close right door for Chica & sometimes Freddy, if you die that's okay you can restart the night or take a break & watch Markiplier do it,

This game is great.
It runs on probably anything (there're limitations, ok? btw. playing this on Bazzite (linux) without any problems). 
It is super simple (that said, Freddy and Foxy are a bit confusing and made the game frustrating, so I had to use a guide on Steam forums - meh). Fun. Pretty scary (when it comes to it). Not super hard to beat (it takes a bit of practise).

Only things I would complain about are: the dated state of the game (with a stable full price tag), which shows especially in the menu (there're no settings) and generally it just shows (on resolution etc. etc.) and again the lack of informations on some of mechanics of the game, which make it just frustrating to play (trial and error without a clue is not fun).

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game lacks proper tutorials or explanations for its mechanics, leaving players to figure things out through trial and error or external guides.

citations.review_text:
To me, by far the easiest out the bunch with knowledge on them all. As a new player though, this is tough to figure out by rawdogging it. 

Tips of advice for freddy and foxy; to delay foxy from leaving pirates cove, you don't have to check on his camera, just any camera in general will have the same stalling effect on him. 

Also, from nights 3-6, keeping an eye on freddy, also foxy every once in a while to check his stage, but mainly freddy to stall him and prevent him reaching your office. Use your office lights for bonnie and chica. It's quite useless tracking them on the cameras. Just keep freddy stalled in the later nights, and keep an eye on foxy here and there and you should be good. 

I won't provide help for 20202020 as it's much funner if you figure it out yourself. Try not to google any methods, but if you have to, that's fine. Use it as a last resort to squeeze as much fun out the game as possible.
